entries.meaning: May those two beneficent scions of Raghu grant us devotion: one lovely as jasmine and the other as a blue lotus, both immensely strong and abodes of insight, rich in splendour, excellent archers praised by the Vedas and dear to herds of cows and Brahmins; they assume human forms through māyā, wear true dharma as armour, and travel the path intent upon finding Sītā.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

words: one lovely as jasmine and the other as a blue lotus, both immensely strong
the two praised by the Vedas
the two dear to herds of cows and Brahmins
the two assuming human forms through māyā
the two eminent scions of Raghu
the two whose armour is true dharma
the two intent upon finding Sītā

entries.meaning: Blessed are those virtuous people who continually drink the nectar of Śrī Rāma's name—arisen from the ocean of Brahman, imperishable and destructive of the Kali age's impurity; forever radiant in the exquisite moon of glorious Śambhu's mouth; medicine for the disease of worldly existence, a giver of joy, and the very life of glorious Jānakī.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

words: arisen from the ocean of Brahman
destroying the impurity of the Kali age
in the exquisite moon of glorious Śambhu's mouth
medicine for the disease of worldly existence
the very life of glorious Jānakī
the nectar of Śrī Rāma's name

entries.meaning: Knowing it to be the birthplace of liberation, a mine of knowledge and a destroyer of sin—the place where Śambhu and Bhavānī dwell—why should one not serve that Kāśī?
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: When the entire host of gods was burning, he drank the terrible poison. Dull mind, why do you not worship him? Who is as compassionate as Śaṅkara?
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.
